59747551.s: Kaab bin Al Ashraf Fort is one of the old forts of Madinah and is considered one of its most important and prominent historic fortresses. It was built 14 centuries ago and covered an area of about 2,000 square metres. It consists of 20 rooms and eight watchtowers, although a large part of the fort has been destroyed and has disappeared over the ages. Remains of the fort still stand and are visited by many locals and tourists interested in archaeology and history.

59660189.t: Al Manakha Heritage Museum in Umluj
59660189.s: Al Manakha Heritage Museum was established in 2015 by Dr Musaad Salama Al Fayidi in the city of Umluj. It has an exhibition covering 8,000 square metres, and its permanent collection includes important antiquities, a historical library, clothing, folk heritage, old cars and many other items that reflect the long history of Umluj. The museum is named Al Manakha because camels would "tanukh", meaning kneel down, beside this site, as it lies next to an ancient spring.

This makes it a favourite destination for boat trips, snorkelling, diving and watching marine life.

59660166.s: Jabal Hassan Island lies on the north-western coast of Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea and belongs administratively to Umluj governorate in the Tabuk region. It is about 18 kilometres from the shore of the city of Umluj. It is named Jabal Hassan after the Hasasinah clan of the Juhaynah tribe, and in the past it was a passage for ships between Egypt and the Arabian Peninsula and Jordan.
